newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu's ill health delays Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's ill health delays Zaire peace talks.

text.p: Zairean peace talks on board a South African navy ship were being held up because President Mobutu Sese Seko was too sick to climb or be flown on board, officials said on Friday.

"The problem is the steep metal steps," said one South African official on board the Outeniqua, the supply ship moored in a Congolese port and due to take Mobutu and his rebel rival Laurent Kabila out to sea for their first talks.

Zaire's Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda said doctors had also advised the ailing, cancer-stricken Mobutu against being flown on board by helicopter because the vibrations would be bad for him. But Kamanda remained optimistic.
"The president is going to come," he told reporters on the ship, where South African President Nelson Mandela was waiting to chair the talks on ending Zaire's seven-month civil war.
He said Mobutu, who flew by plane from Kinshasa earlier on Friday and was waiting at the airport of the coastal city of Pointe Noire, was in good spirits.
The Outeniqua was due to leave Pointe Noire and sail south for two hours to pick Kabila up off the coast of Angola, where he was waiting in the capital Luanda.
